Indikator 10b is an official Danish quality indicator for acute surgery that measures 30-day mortality among patients with a [[charlson-comorbiditets-indeks|Charlson Comorbiditets indeks]] score of 1 or 2 [^src1]. It is featured in the final public version of the Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen) from February 2024, published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Program [^src1]. The indicator and its supplementary version form the foundation for statistical analyses of post-operative mortality, stratified by the patients' pre-existing disease burden [^src1]. 

During the analyzed period, the indicator analysis included a total of 1,086 patients [^src1]. Of this cohort, 11.2% (95% CI: 9.4–13.3) died within 30 days of their operation [^src1]. The integration of the [[charlson-comorbiditets-indeks|Charlson Comorbiditets indeks]] into the definition of Indikator 10b serves as a central tool for risk adjustment, reflecting a systematic effort to ensure comparable, high-quality, and clinically relevant measurements within the Danish healthcare system [^src1].
